#+title: Replay selected immutable tests

* Capture, inspect, run
Run in the captured immutable test-source directory with the selected SDK's
direct bin/bl launcher. A cold receiver keeps mutable caller definitions out:

#+begin_src sh
/absolute/selected-sdk/bin/bl --cold artifacts replay-capture /absolute/options.json /absolute/capsule.json
/absolute/selected-sdk/bin/bl --cold artifacts replay-plan /absolute/capsule.json
/absolute/selected-sdk/bin/bl --cold artifacts replay /absolute/capsule.json /absolute/result.json
#+end_src

replay-capture hashes selected inputs, observes actual SDK/runtime/tools and
retains their closures. replay-plan verifies the capture against actual current
observations and returns admission data. replay runs through the ordinary
isolated selected-file test path and writes its structured result to RESULT_JSON.

Keep the original capture file. Its exact {capsule,custody} wrapper contains
immutable test metadata and the retained-root record. The result file contains
the updated capsule, fresh custody, aggregate counters and actual outcome and
qualification receipts. It is a report, rather than a replacement capture input.
Test stdout can appear on the terminal; machine consumers read RESULT_JSON.

Live execution supports explicit .bl files. The DATA capsule also accepts
literate and ExUnit selections; those require their own live receiver integration.
Qualification covers selected tests only. The product is retained and checked;
product activation and proof that tests consumed its compiled code belong to
separate verified runtime operations.

* Options and APIs
OPTIONS_JSON is a JSON object using these fields:

| Field | Meaning |
| product / source | Actual immutable product and its Source root |
| test-source | Optional immutable test/fixture root; defaults to source |
| tests | Nonempty explicit relative test filenames |
| inputs | Optional explicit relative support filenames |
| cwd | Relative directory inside test-source; defaults to . |
| tool-names | Optional names resolved through pinned startup tools |
| reproduction | Optional existing artifact/capsule! descriptor or wrapper |

Use actual top-level /nix/store addresses for the three input roots. SDK,
compiler/build/native identities and tool paths come from runtime observation.
Options cannot supply argv, commands, environment maps or execution grants.
Only absent fields select defaults; explicit false/null for path/list options
refuses. Source identities do not capture mutable databases, credentials, time,
randomness, remote services or process interleavings.

The library capture API accepts equivalent string or keyword fields:

#+begin_src clojure
(ns example.capture (:require [artifact.replay-runner :as live]))

(live/capture!
  {:product selected-product :source product-source
   :test-source immutable-test-source :cwd "."
   :tests ["test/example_test.bl"]
   :inputs ["test/fixtures/example.json"] :tool-names ["z3"]}
  private-custody-parent)
#+end_src

| API | Result |
| artifact.replay-runner/observe! [] or [tool-names] | Actual sdk/runtime/tools observations |
| artifact.replay-runner/capture! [options custody-parent] | capsule and retained custody |
| artifact.replay-runner/assert-clean! [capsule] | Read-only clean-context evidence or refusal |
| artifact.replay-runner/run! [capsule custody-parent] | Updated capsule, custody, aggregate, status and receipt arrays |
| artifact.replay/capture!, validate, plan!, attach-outcome, attach-qualification | Bounded DATA operations; see artifact-replay.org |

The capture example can construct data in application code. Live run! requires
a clean receiver: a script that defines project vars is not a clean SDK context.
The native CLI supplies the file-oriented integration.

* Verify the actual SDK
The selected SDK must be an immutable store object with a bounded sdk
artifact.json. Its canonical image/priv must equal Tiers/priv_root, and its
bootstrap seed must equal Bootstrap/seed_dir. Bootstrap/packaged_keys! checks
floor bytes and loaded stable members. Compiler/build boot keys must match
verified packaged and current keys. LazyMemo/runtime_identity! supplies the
loaded-native identity.

A mutable checkout or an unrelated extracted portable floor refuses this
physical binding. Extracted-drop support requires a verified runtime mapping
to the selected SDK. Equal environment strings or recorded labels supply no
such proof. Tools resolve through artifact-process/tool and are canonical
immutable executable files; observation hashes their actual bytes.

* Use a clean receiver
assert-clean! runs before retention, immediately before the selected test hook
and after execution. It inspects existing runtime evidence:

- Env/env_id is global and Env/chain exactly [global]. Project realm declarations
  and active loader realms refuse.
- Env/load_paths, Env/search_paths, explicit process loader lists, BEAM_LISP_PATH
  and captured deferred-require paths resolve inside captured source/test-source
  or the verified SDK priv root. Missing SDK Source directories are allowed only
  beneath an existing physical SDK ancestor; application roots must exist.
- BEAM_LISP_CODE_PATH additions refuse. Actual BEAM search directories resolve
  into /nix/store; mutable ebins and relative current-directory entries refuse.
- AOT/sdk_runtime_inventory! authenticates SDK code and routes. Every namespace
  from declarations or visible var slots has verified SDK-unit provenance or
  authenticated bootstrap-manifest membership. Floor membership uses the
  manifest's namespace mapping and exact loaded bytes or verified forwarder
  routes. Empty namespaces require zero definitions and no own vars.
- Env/definition_context remains stable during inspection.

Current source_path cannot establish where an already loaded value came from.
Preloaded non-SDK definitions therefore refuse even if a same-named immutable
file is available. The predicate supplies evidence, not execution authority or
a way to reset a caller realm.

Loader/with_search_dir pins immutable test-source as the sole ambient/fixed
Source root. Env/capture carries that context into the existing ward workers.
Selected tests use their exact absolute filenames. Source dependencies need to
resolve within that arrangement. Arbitrary multi-root project resolver adoption
requires a verified fresh-receiver integration.

* Execute and record
run! rechecks the capsule and actual observations, retains all closures, then
checks again before calling bl.test/run-selected-data!. That hook shares the
normal isolated runner's source extraction, coherence gate and ward execution.
Request-local cwd/argv use BeamLisp's existing bindings. No parallel executor
or metadata-derived execution grant is introduced.

After execution, the complete selected file count, actual SDK/runtime/tools and
captured inputs must remain consistent. A successful nonempty run records a
passing outcome. A successful empty run is incomplete. Nonzero exit/coherence
refusal stays nonpassing even with zero assertion totals. Exceptions and changed
post-run identities refuse passing qualification.

Receipts contain fixed labels and bounded numeric aggregates. Test output,
exception strings, credentials and arbitrary environment data stay outside the
persisted receipt. Their array shapes are:

#+begin_src text
[1, "selected-test-outcome", binding, status,
 [tests, pass, fail, error, files, ok, exit], "bl.test/run-selected-data!"]
[1, "selected-test-qualification", binding, status,
 "selected-tests-only", outcomeReceiptDigest]
#+end_src

Each attachment's receiptDigest is SHA256 of Jason/encode! of its returned array.
Keep both arrays with the updated capsule. Stored reports are observations;
compatibility, full SDK promotion and application-data restore require their
own evidence and protocols.

* Retention and publication
The CLI derives its private retention parent from pinned framework cache/home.
The library takes an existing private canonical parent owned by the operator.
Each capture/run creates a fresh mode 0700 child and retains SDK, product,
source, test-source and required tool closures using fixed bounded nix-store
operations through the existing process adapter. Existing objects are required.
Roots persist until their custody directory is removed. Partial retention
failures remove partial roots; later failures conservatively retain custody.

The existing artifact writer claim covers capture/execution through publication.
Existing output files refuse before work begins. A mode 0600 exclusive temporary
file is synchronized, closed and atomically hardlinked to the new destination;
publication never overwrites another file. An external collision after execution
can prevent publication while retained roots remain available for inspection.

JSON ingress accepts regular files without symlink components, bounded to
8 MiB, 64 structural levels and 65536 nodes including object keys. Lexical
preflight bounds structure before ordered-object decoding. Every duplicate raw
field, including identically decoded escaped names, refuses before map
construction. Closed replay schemas also reject unknown or duplicate normalized
fields. Hash reads use bounded chunks; see [[file:artifact-replay.org][capsule bounds]].

* Qualification controls
Qualification requires the actual target SDK and its lifecycle/receiver controls.
Exercise nonempty pass, failing assertions, zero-total coherence refusal and
empty success; compare counters against the ordinary isolated test path.
Check actual floor/tool/input mismatches and recompute both receipt digests.
Verify retention before execution, private output modes, duplicate JSON refusal
and existing-output refusal before tests start.

A test requiring a mutable caller dependency or preloaded project var must
refuse before execution. Include mutable ebin/current-directory paths, inherited
realms, deferred mutable roots and immutable-looking source paths for preloaded
values. A clean SDK positive case establishes the intended receiver boundary;
it does not certify complete failure reproduction or broader product promotion.
